description: Explicit CE->CPI scope treatments for the 58 Milestone-1 exception UCCs. Every exception UCC is claimed by exactly one rule. Rules are evidence-bearing: each records the authoritative BLS source that supports the treatment, the transformation formula where one exists, the assumptions taken, and the validation test that must pass.
attribution: UCC codes and titles, ELI codes and titles, the CE hierarchical grouping (stub) files, the CPI Handbook of Methods, and the CE-CPI concordance are published by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics. The grouping of UCCs into the scope rules below, the rule identifiers, and the DMI computation-node assignments are DMI research metadata and are not a BLS product.
governing_constraints: Milestone 2 Section 5.2: OUT_OF_SCOPE may be used only where authoritative evidence supports exclusion from the selected Track-A CPI consumption universe. Absence of a row in the concordance is not, by itself, sufficient evidence. Every OUT_OF_SCOPE rule below therefore cites a positive scope statement from a BLS methodological source, not merely the absence of a concordance row.
Milestone 2 Section 5.3: a classification must never be invented merely to drive unresolved expenditure to zero. UNRESOLVED_v0_2 is retained deliberately.

Milestone 2 Section 6.5: owner shelter financing and owner shelter capital expenditure must not coexist with rental-equivalence expenditure. Rules whose effect is coupled to the Track-A shelter transformation are marked review_status PROPOSED and take effect only jointly with the Track-A rental-equivalence rule.
Milestone 2 Section 19.3: this registry does not normalize weights and does not construct DMI weights.

rule_type_semantics.EXCLUDE: Source expenditure leaves the CPI-compatible basis entirely. It remains in the CE-outlay basis and must be reported in the out_of_scope reconciliation column.
rule_type_semantics.REPLACE: Source expenditure is removed and substituted by a different, CPI-adjusted expenditure concept. The replacement amount is not required to equal the removed amount.
rule_type_semantics.COMBINE: Two or more source UCCs are summed into a single successor concept that carries the concordance mapping.
rule_type_semantics.REASSIGN: Source expenditure is retained in full but is allocated to one or more DMI computation nodes other than the one a naive CE-parent reading would give.
rule_type_semantics.RETAIN: Source expenditure is retained and mapped unchanged. Not used in this registry: retained UCCs are not Milestone-1 exceptions.
rule_type_semantics.UNRESOLVED: No authoritative treatment was found. Expenditure is neither retained nor excluded; it is carried explicitly as unresolved.

evidence_strength_scale.STRONG: A current BLS methodological publication states the treatment explicitly and the affected UCCs are unambiguously instances of the stated concept.
evidence_strength_scale.MODERATE: A BLS methodological publication states a principle that determines the treatment, but BLS does not name the affected UCCs; or the naming source is a superseded BLS document whose principle is corroborated by current structural evidence.
evidence_strength_scale.WEAK: Only structural or circumstantial evidence. Not sufficient for OUT_OF_SCOPE under Section 5.2 and not used for any EXCLUDE rule here.

CPI_HOM_CONCEPTS.title: Handbook of Methods, Consumer Price Index: Concepts, section 'Scope and exclusions'
quoted_passages: The CPI covers the consumption sector of the U.S. economy, which is defined as the purchase of goods and services for use by households. Consequently, the CPI excludes investment items, such as stocks, bonds, real estate, and business expenses.
Purchases of houses, antiques, and collectibles are viewed as investment expenditures and therefore excluded.
Interest costs and finance charges are also out-of-scope.
The CPI excludes income tax and other direct taxes; however, it does include the effects of changes in sales taxes and other indirect taxes paid on consumer products.
The CPI treats any changes to fees that the government charges for items, such as admission to a national park, as in-scope changes in price.

CASEY_2010.title: An Overview of the CPI's Requirements of the Consumer Expenditure Survey
CASEY_2010.author: Casey, W.
CASEY_2010.tier: 4 (BLS methodological paper). Used for principles and for corroborating structural evidence. Its Appendix B UCC lists describe a superseded CE vintage and are never used on their own to determine a current mapping.
quoted_passages: CPI's expenditure scope is net out-of-pocket-expense for market goods and services.
Investments like stocks, bonds, real estate, business expenses, and life insurance are considered non-consumption by the CPI.
Illegal goods, gambling winnings and losses, fines, cash gifts, child support, alimony payments, and interest payments are also excluded.

There are several exceptions to the net out-of-pocket expense approach: owned housing, maintenance and repair of owned housing, and major appliances for owned housing are adjusted from net out-of-pocket expense to eliminate investment elements.
Owner expenditures on major appliances and home maintenance and repair are based on the corresponding mean expenditures of renters and likelihood of renters to purchase those types of appliances.
Appendix B note 1: CE collects food at home while on vacation expenditures as a separate category. For CPI use, these expenditures are allocated across all food expenditure classes.
Appendix B note 2: In order to price the rental equivalence of secondary homes and timeshares, CPI uses a factor to account for the consumption portion of a homeowner's total expenditure.
Appendix B note 3: It is required that CPI reduce the homeowners insurance weight to reflect only the renter's part of the owner's expenditure. The factor applied is 43%.
Appendix B note 4: Renter UCCs are paired with homeowner UCCs for calculation of rental equivalence adjustments.
Appendix B note 5: Maintenance to one's home can be considered an investment. For this reason, an allocation factor is applied to remove investment expense from the total consumption expenditure.

CE_CPI_CONCORDANCE_ARCHIVE.title: Archived CE-CPI concordance vintages (2020, 2022, 2024, 2025 publications)
CE_CPI_CONCORDANCE_ARCHIVE.tier: 5 (archived BLS documents). Used only as negative/corroborating historical evidence, never to determine a current mapping.
CE_CPI_CONCORDANCE_ARCHIVE.finding: Across five concordance vintages spanning 2020 to the pinned August-2026 file, only 2 of the 58 Milestone-1 exception UCCs ever carried a row: 270104 (ED041, 2020 vintage only) and 950024 (TF011, 2020/2022/2024 vintages). The other 56 have never been mapped in any vintage examined. This makes the absence a stable multi-year pattern rather than a lag in the current file, which is separately confirmed by the fact that 11 of the 16 UCCs newly introduced in CE quarter 2024-Q2 are already mapped in the pinned concordance.

OWNER_RENTER_COUNTERPART_TEST.description: A reproducible test over the 2024 CE stub and the pinned concordance. It evaluates Casey Appendix B note 4 ('Renter UCCs are paired with homeowner UCCs for calculation of rental equivalence adjustments') against the actual mapping pattern of the owned-dwellings and rented-dwellings maintenance branches.
OWNER_RENTER_COUNTERPART_TEST.result_rented_dwellings: Every maintenance and repair commodity and service UCC under RNTDWELL is mapped, with exactly three exceptions: 230144 (home warranties, introduced 2024-Q2), 990920 (materials for additions/finishing basements/remodeling), and 790690 (construction materials for jobs not started).
OWNER_RENTER_COUNTERPART_TEST.result_owned_dwellings: Under OWNDWELL, an owner maintenance UCC is mapped if and only if a renter UCC expressing the same concept exists. Mapped owner/renter pairs: 240112/240111, 240122/240121, 240212/240211, 240222/240221, 240312/240311, 240322/240321, 320612/320611, 320625/320624, 320632/320631, 230142/230141, 230112->HP043 alongside 230150->HP043, 220121->HD011 alongside 350110->HD011. Unmapped owner UCCs having no renter counterpart: 230113 (plumbing service), 230114 (heat/AC/electrical service), 230115 (roofing service), 230151 (other repair service), 240213 (roof and gutter materials), 230901 (property management), 210901 (ground rent), 220901 (parking).
OWNER_RENTER_COUNTERPART_TEST.interpretation: The CE renter branch carries a single generic maintenance-service code (230150) while the CE owner branch is split into structure-system trades. CPI weights the owner side from the renter counterpart per Casey notes 3 to 5. Where no renter counterpart exists, there is no consumption portion to pair and the owner amount is treated as investment in the structure. This is the documented basis for OS_CPI_OWNER_STRUCTURE_INVESTMENT_v0_1.
OWNER_RENTER_COUNTERPART_TEST.known_exception_to_the_pattern: 340911 (management and upkeep services for security, owned) is mapped to HP090 'Unsampled Household Operations' without an explicit renter counterpart. HP090 is a residual 'unsampled' ELI, so this does not contradict the pairing principle for sampled ELIs, but it is recorded here rather than suppressed.

TRIP_FOOD_NODE_INVARIANCE.description: Casey Appendix B note 1 states that vacation food expenditure is allocated across all food expenditure classes using special adjustment factors that BLS does not publish. The DMI node assignment is nonetheless determinate.
TRIP_FOOD_NODE_INVARIANCE.result: Every ELI prefix reachable from the CE food groups (FA through FT and FV) resolves to node FOOD in eli_to_node_map_v0_1, and both alcohol prefixes (FW, FX) resolve to node ALCOHOLIC_BEVERAGES. The allocation is therefore node-invariant: whatever weights BLS uses internally, the destination node is unchanged.

VEHICLE_REGISTRATION_COMBINE_IDENTITY.description: CE 2024 Interview PUMD record-level identity supporting the COMBINE transformation.
VEHICLE_REGISTRATION_COMBINE_IDENTITY.result: In the 2024 Interview MTBI files, UCC 510115 equals UCC 520110 plus UCC 950024 on 4785 of 4785 records (100.0%). Aggregate check: 894639 + 383417 = 1278056.
VEHICLE_REGISTRATION_COMBINE_IDENTITY.corroboration: The 2020, 2022 and 2024 concordance vintages map 520111 + 520112 + 950024 to TF011. The 2025 and pinned August-2026 vintages map the single successor code 510115 to TF011. The CPI concept is unchanged across the CE recoding.
VEHICLE_REGISTRATION_COMBINE_IDENTITY.not_reproduced_reason: The record-level identity is asserted from the 2024 CE Interview PUMD MTBI files, which are not distributed with this repository, so no committed test reproduces it. The concordance-side claim the COMBINE rule depends on, that 510115 resolves to the single ELI TF011, is reproduced by tests/test_detailed_inflation_milestone_2.py::TestStructuralEvidence::test_vehicle_registration_combine_destination. Reproducing the 4785-of-4785 record identity as a regression test is outstanding work.

These three UCCs are absent from Casey Appendix B's UCC lists, which is consistent with their being distributed into other classes rather than carried as their own mapped line. rules.transformation_formula: E_node(FOOD) += E(190903) + E(190904); E_node(ALCOHOLIC_BEVERAGES) += E(200900). No amount is created or destroyed.

See structural_evidence.TRIP_FOOD_NODE_INVARIANCE.
Alcohol purchased on trips is assumed to follow the same allocation mechanism as trip food. Casey attaches the same footnote marker to the alcohol groups FW and FX, which supports this.

source_document_titles: Handbook of Methods, Consumer Price Index: Concepts, 'Scope and exclusions'
An Overview of the CPI's Requirements of the Consumer Expenditure Survey
rules.evidence_notes: Two independent grounds, either of which is sufficient. First, scope: the CPI Handbook of Methods states 'Interest costs and finance charges are also out-of-scope', and mortgage interest, home-equity-loan interest and HELOC interest are interest by name and by CE stub placement (all eight UCCs sit under OWNMORTG or OWNVMORT, 'Mortgage interest and charges'). Second, method: Casey 2010 states that owned housing is 'adjusted from net out-of-pocket expense to eliminate investment elements', and the CPI prices owner shelter by rental equivalence rather than by the owner's financing outlay, so mortgage interest is displaced by the Track-A rental-equivalence concept rather than double counted.
assumptions: Late fees on a mortgage payment (830111, 830112) are treated as a charge on the credit instrument, so they follow the interest treatment. This is the weaker member of the family: BLS does not name these codes, and they were introduced in CE quarter 2024-Q2. Their combined All-CU materiality is 21 million dollars, or 0.0003 percent of the basis, so the classification risk is negligible. Recorded here rather than silently absorbed.

This rule removes owner financing expenditure. Per Milestone 2 Section 6.5 it must not be applied independently of the Track-A rental-equivalence rule, or owner shelter cost would be removed without a replacement concept.
rules.suppression_note: 830112 (late fee, owned vacation) is suppressed for All Consumer Units and for four quintiles. Its published sibling 830111 is 21 million dollars, so the suppressed amount is bounded far below materiality.
rules.review_blocker: Takes effect only jointly with the Track-A rental-equivalence rule (Milestone 2 Section 6.5). Pending the PUMD annual-weighting and quintile benchmark validation required before the Track-A shelter rule is finalized.

track_b.rationale: This expenditure is out of scope for Track A because the CPI prices owner-occupied shelter by rental equivalence and treats mortgage interest as the cost of an investment asset. Under a household-payments concept the opposite holds: contractual mortgage interest, home-equity interest and mortgage late fees are contemporaneous cash outlays that a household must meet, and the BLS Homeowner Cost Index research series retains mortgage interest for exactly this reason. This is the single largest concept difference between the two tracks.
price_index_needed: A mortgage interest cost index. No published CPI series measures this. It would have to be constructed from a contract mortgage interest rate series and a loan-balance or house-price series, as the BLS HCI research work does. Constructing it is not authorized in Milestone 2.

A home-equity borrowing rate series for UCCs 220313, 220314, 880110 and 880310, which track a different instrument from first-lien mortgages and would move with short-term rates rather than 30-year mortgage rates.

rules.evidence_notes: CPI Handbook of Methods, Concepts: 'The CPI excludes income tax and other direct taxes; however, it does include the effects of changes in sales taxes and other indirect taxes paid on consumer products.' Residential property tax is a direct tax on the owner. Independently, Casey 2010 establishes that owner housing cost is converted to rental equivalence to eliminate investment elements, which displaces property tax as a separately weighted item.
assumptions: Residential property tax is classified as a direct tax rather than an indirect tax on a consumer product. This follows the Handbook's own contrast between direct taxes and 'sales taxes and other indirect taxes paid on consumer products'.

This treatment is deliberately not extended to the vehicle personal property tax (950024). BLS itself bundles that levy into the vehicle registration fee concept and maps it to TF011, and the Handbook states that government fees are in scope. See TR_VEHICLE_REGISTRATION_FEES_v0_1.
Per Milestone 2 Section 6.5 this rule must not be applied independently of the Track-A rental-equivalence rule.
rules.review_blocker: Takes effect only jointly with the Track-A rental-equivalence rule (Milestone 2 Section 6.5).

track_b.rationale: Out of scope for Track A because the CPI treats residential property tax as a cost of owning the asset rather than a price of shelter consumption. Under a payments concept property tax is a recurring compulsory outlay tied to occupancy of the dwelling and is retained, consistent with the BLS HCI treatment.
price_index_needed: An effective residential property tax index, i.e. assessed value multiplied by the applicable millage rate. No published CPI series measures this and no BLS series is pinned for it in this milestone.

rules.evidence_notes: Four independent legs. (1) The pinned concordance maps CE successor code 510115 'Veh Registration Incl Prop Tax' to TF011. (2) CE 2024 Interview PUMD: 510115 equals 520110 plus 950024 on 4785 of 4785 records, 100.0 percent, aggregate 894639 + 383417 = 1278056. (3) The 2020, 2022 and 2024 concordance vintages mapped the predecessor codes 520111 + 520112 + 950024 to the same TF011; only the CE coding changed, not the CPI concept. (4) BLS ELI definition for TF011: 'Includes the price for initial issue and renewal of private passenger vehicle registration, operator license, and learner permit as required by the state government... Includes all fees and surcharges which must be paid simultaneously with registration and licensing.' This also resolves the apparent tension with the CPI's exclusion of direct taxes: BLS classifies the vehicle personal property levy as part of a registration fee, and the Handbook states government fees are in scope.
rules.transformation_formula: E(510115, p) = E(520110, p) + E(950024, p) for each population p. The combined amount maps to ELI TF011 and thence to node TRANSPORT_SERVICES.
assumptions: 510115 does not appear in cx.item because it carries PUBFLAG=1 ('Not published') in the CE microdata. It is therefore a CPI-adjusted PUMD UCC rather than a published CE UCC, and its absence from the published item file is expected, not an error.
The record-level identity was verified on 2024 Interview data. The rule asserts the identity for 2024 only; a later CE vintage must be re-verified before the rule version is carried forward.
Combining at the population level assumes the identity holds within each income quintile, which follows from its holding on every individual record.

source_document_titles: Handbook of Methods, Consumer Price Index, Appendix 2: Content of CPI Entry Level Items, TB022 'Alternative motor fuels'
Measuring Price Change in the CPI: Motor fuel
Consumer Expenditure Surveys hierarchical grouping file CE-HG-Integ-2024.txt, parent GASFUEL
rules.evidence_notes: Milestone 2 Section 11 forbids assigning EV charging by analogy alone and requires an authoritative treatment. Two current BLS sources name electricity as a motor fuel explicitly. Appendix 2, TB022 'Alternative motor fuels': 'All automotive motor fuels other than gasoline and diesel. Includes biodiesel, ethanol, electric, CNG (compressed natural gas) and hydrogen that is sold for use in consumer automobiles for use on public roads/streets.' The CPI motor fuel factsheet: 'The other motor fuels index is composed of automotive diesel fuel and alternative motor fuels such as Ethanol..., biodiesel, natural gas, and electricity that is sold for use in consumer automobiles.' The CPI item structure places TB022 under SETB02 'Other motor fuels' within SETB 'Motor fuel'. On the CE side, 470311 sits under stub parent GASFUEL 'Gasoline and other fuels' alongside 470111, 470112 and 470113. The CE question wording (VOPELEC) restricts 470311 to charging away from home, so it does not overlap residential electricity (HF011).
rules.transformation_formula: E_node(MOTOR_FUEL) += E(470311). No amount is created or destroyed.
assumptions: BLS does not publish a concordance row for 470311 in any of the five vintages examined. TB022's expenditure weight is instead carried by 470111 and 470113 under the special adjustment factors of trailer note (1). The concordance is therefore acting as a weight-source mapping here, not as a scope statement, and its silence on 470311 does not place EV charging out of scope. The two Handbook and factsheet quotations are what establish scope.
No double count arises: 470111, 470113 and 470311 are disjoint CE leaves that reconcile to the published GASFUEL parent.
Away-from-home charging only. Home charging is measured inside residential electricity (HF011) and is not affected by this rule.
open_questions: BLS has published no statement on how, or whether, 470311 enters the CPI weight for TB022.
BLS has published no EV-charging price-collection methodology, and there is no published CPI series more granular than SETB02 'Other motor fuels'.
The date at which 'electric' was added to the TB022 definition could not be established: the Internet Archive availability and CDX APIs returned HTTP 503 throughout the attempt.
rules.evidence_strength_note: Scope is established by tier-1 current BLS sources naming electricity as an alternative motor fuel, which is STRONG. It is graded MODERATE overall because BLS does not name UCC 470311 anywhere, so the link from this specific CE code to TB022 rests on the CE stub placement and the away-from-home question wording rather than on a BLS statement.

rules.evidence_notes: Milestone 2 Section 12 forbids inferring a treatment from the CE parent category 'Housing' alone, so this rule rests on a stated BLS principle plus a reproducible structural test. Principle: the CPI 'excludes investment items, such as stocks, bonds, real estate'; Casey 2010 states that 'owned housing, maintenance and repair of owned housing, and major appliances for owned housing are adjusted from net out-of-pocket expense to eliminate investment elements', that 'Owner expenditures on major appliances and home maintenance and repair are based on the corresponding mean expenditures of renters', that 'Renter UCCs are paired with homeowner UCCs' (note 4), that homeowners insurance is reduced 'to reflect only the renter's part of the owner's expenditure. The factor applied is 43%' (note 3), and that 'Maintenance to one's home can be considered an investment. For this reason, an allocation factor is applied to remove investment expense from the total consumption expenditure' (note 5). Structural test: see structural_evidence.OWNER_RENTER_COUNTERPART_TEST. Every owner maintenance UCC that has a renter counterpart is mapped in the pinned concordance; the eight UCCs above are precisely the owner-side codes that have no renter counterpart to supply a consumption portion. The owner/renter tenure split is therefore not itself the exclusion criterion, which is confirmed by the many owner codes that are mapped (230112, 240112, 240212, 240222, 240312, 240322, 320612, 320625, 320632, 230142, 220121).
assumptions: Ground rent (210901) is a payment for the use of land. Land is real estate, which the Handbook excludes as an investment item.

Parking at an owned dwelling (220901) is treated as part of the owner shelter cost displaced by rental equivalence, not as a separable transport service. It sits under CE stub parent OWNEXPEN, inside Shelter, not under Transportation.

Property management (230901) is treated as an owner shelter cost displaced by rental equivalence. Note that 340911 'Management and upkeep services for security (owned)' is mapped to HP090, an 'unsampled' residual ELI; the two are not the same concept, but this is the closest counter-instance and is recorded in structural_evidence.OWNER_RENTER_COUNTERPART_TEST.known_exception_to_the_pattern rather than suppressed.
Per Milestone 2 Section 6.5 this rule must not be applied independently of the Track-A rental-equivalence rule.
rules.evidence_strength_note: The exclusion principle is stated by BLS, but BLS does not name these eight UCCs. The assignment rests on the reproducible owner/renter counterpart test rather than on a BLS enumeration, so it is graded MODERATE and carries review_status PROPOSED.
rules.review_blocker: Takes effect only jointly with the Track-A rental-equivalence rule (Milestone 2 Section 6.5). This is the largest MODERATE-evidence exclusion in the registry at 3.4 percent of basis and should receive explicit reviewer attention.

track_b.rationale: Out of scope for Track A because the CPI weights owner maintenance from the renter counterpart and these eight UCCs have no renter counterpart, so under rental equivalence they are absorbed into the value of the structure. Under a payments concept they are ordinary recurring maintenance and occupancy outlays, not capital acquisition, and are retained. This includes ground rent (210901) and parking (220901), which are occupancy payments rather than works on the structure.
price_index_needed: Existing CPI household maintenance and repair services indexes can supply price change for 230113, 230114, 230115, 230151 and 240213, because the renter counterpart items are already sampled by the CPI; only the weight, not the price series, is missing.
No published CPI series is identified for property management fees (230901) or for ground rent (210901). These would remain price-source gaps under Track B.

Consumer Expenditure Surveys hierarchical grouping file CE-HG-Integ-2024.txt, branch Shelter > Other lodging > Owned vacation homes
rules.evidence_notes: Casey Appendix B note 2: 'In order to price the rental equivalence of secondary homes and timeshares, CPI uses a factor to account for the consumption portion of a homeowner's total expenditure.' Structural corroboration: every single UCC under the CE stub branch 'Shelter > Other lodging > Owned vacation homes' (containers OWVHOME, OWVEXPEN, OWVREPSV, OWVREPSP, OWVMISC, OWVMNAGE, OWNVMORT) is unmapped in the pinned concordance, while the corresponding primary-residence codes are largely mapped (for example 240112, 240212, 240222, 240312, 240322, 320612, 320625, 320632, 220121, 340911). The branch is excluded as a whole, not item by item, which is what a single aggregate consumption factor applied to total secondary-home owner expenditure would produce.
rules.transformation_formula: Removed: sum of E(u) over the source UCCs. Added: the Track-A secondary-residence rental-equivalence amount, which is supplied by the Track-A shelter rule and is not computed here. Per the Milestone 2 amendment, the replacement amount is not required to equal the removed amount.
assumptions: This is classified REPLACE rather than EXCLUDE. BLS documents that secondary-residence owner cost is priced by rental equivalence, so the expenditure is displaced by a different concept rather than removed from the consumption universe. The competing reading, that these are simply excluded as investment in real estate, cannot be ruled out from the published record; it is recorded here as the documented alternative. Under either reading the amount leaves the CE-outlay basis, so the reconciliation identity is unaffected. What differs is only whether the amount is reported as replaced or as out of scope.

Owned-vacation-home mortgage interest (220312, 220314, 830112, 880310) and property tax (220212) are members of this same CE branch but are claimed by OS_CPI_MORTGAGE_INTEREST_AND_CHARGES_v0_1 and OS_CPI_RESIDENTIAL_PROPERTY_TAX_v0_1 respectively, because those have independent STRONG scope grounds that do not depend on the secondary-residence argument. Each UCC is claimed by exactly one rule.

990940 'Material for finishing basements and remodeling rooms (owned vacation)' is a member of this CE branch but is claimed by OS_CPI_CAPITAL_IMPROVEMENT_v0_1, so that the capital-improvement concept is treated identically across all three tenures.
Per Milestone 2 Section 6.5 this rule must not be applied independently of the Track-A rental-equivalence rule.
rules.suppression_note: 320633 is suppressed for All Consumer Units and several quintiles; 8 of 15 UCCs are suppressed in Q1. The suppressed members are the smallest codes in a branch whose published total is 0.18 percent of basis, so the exposure is bounded well below materiality.
rules.review_blocker: Takes effect only jointly with the Track-A rental-equivalence rule (Milestone 2 Section 6.5). The Milestone 2 amendment requires the PUMD annual-weighting and quintile benchmark validation to pass before Track A is finalized; secondary-residence estimates are noisy and RSE must be carried rather than used to drop these items.

track_b.rationale: Track A replaces these owner outlays with rental equivalence for the secondary residence. A payments concept performs no such substitution: the household's actual outlays on the vacation or secondary home are the contemporaneous payments, so the recorded CE amounts are retained as-is. Track B therefore does not inherit the Track-A replacement and is not blocked by the unresolved rental-equivalence question.
price_index_needed: The same CPI maintenance, repair, insurance and utility component indexes used for the primary-residence counterparts would apply. No secondary-residence-specific CPI series exists, so Track B would have to assume primary-residence price change applies to secondary residences. That assumption is untested here.

source_document_titles: Handbook of Methods, Consumer Price Index: Concepts, 'Scope and exclusions'
An Overview of the CPI's Requirements of the Consumer Expenditure Survey, Appendix B note 5
rules.evidence_notes: The Handbook excludes 'investment items, such as stocks, bonds, real estate' and states that 'Purchases of houses... are viewed as investment expenditures and therefore excluded'. Additions, basement finishing and room remodeling add to the structure rather than maintain it, so they are capital expenditure on real estate. Casey Appendix B note 5 supplies the same principle for home maintenance generally. Decisive structural evidence: this is the only maintenance-commodity concept that is unmapped on all three tenures. The renter branch is otherwise 100 percent mapped (see structural_evidence.OWNER_RENTER_COUNTERPART_TEST), yet 990920 (renter) is unmapped alongside 990930 (owner) and 990940 (owned vacation). Tenure therefore cannot explain the exclusion; the concept does.
assumptions: 790690 'Construction materials for jobs not started' is grouped here on a second ground as well: the materials have been purchased but the job has not been performed, so under the CPI's acquisition framing there is no completed consumption acquisition to price. This is a DMI reading; BLS does not comment on this code.

The boundary between maintenance (in scope, weighted from the renter counterpart) and capital improvement (excluded) is drawn on the CE title wording of these four codes. BLS does not publish an explicit boundary definition.
rules.suppression_note: Computed by dmi_research.detailed_inflation.resolution: 13 of this rule's 24 population cells are suppressed, and in the worst population up to 52.2% of the rule's own possible total is unobserved, above the 25% threshold. Two of the four members (990930, 990940) are suppressed in all six populations. Spec section 16 requires such a rule to find an alternative source, aggregate to a sufficiently stable level, or remain blocked. The disposition here is to aggregate: the rule is not blocked because the EXCLUDE decision rests on the concordance evidence that capital improvement is unmapped on all three tenures, not on the magnitudes, and the magnitudes are bounded from the published BLS parent at no more than 0.0123% of the expenditure basis in any population. The suppressed cells are carried as bounded unknowns and are never coerced to zero. Any future use of this rule must consume it at the rule total, not at the individual UCC, because the individual UCC amounts are not published.

track_b.rationale: This is the one Track-A exclusion that Track B also excludes. Additions, finished basements, remodeled rooms and materials bought for jobs not started are capital acquisition that adds to the asset, not a recurring payment for current housing services. Milestone 2 section 7 requires current expense to be distinguished from capital acquisition, and this rule is where that distinction binds. Note that the labor component of these jobs is not in this rule; only materials UCCs appear as Milestone-1 exceptions.

rules.evidence_notes: No authoritative BLS treatment was found for these eleven UCCs. Per Milestone 2 Section 5.3 no classification is invented for them. Each carries a candidate destination recorded purely as a research lead; candidates are never applied and never enter any reconciliation total.
assumptions: A Diary-versus-Interview source-selection explanation was tested for 300900 and 340913 and rejected: Diary-sourced UCCs are widely mapped in the pinned concordance (190 Diary rows against 434 Interview rows), so the collection instrument alone does not explain the omission.

members.label: Septic tank cleaning (renter), new UCC 2024-Q2
members.note: Probable BLS clerical omission, recorded as an anomaly rather than resolved. Its owner twin 270907 'Septic tank cleaning (owner), new UCC 2024-Q2' maps to HP090, and both predecessors 270901 (renter) and 270902 (owner) map to HP090. BLS mapped both the owner and renter members of the parallel water-softening 2024-Q2 recoding (340421 and 340422). No scope rationale excludes a renter code while including its owner twin, since the investment adjustment runs in the opposite direction. Per Section 5.3 no assignment is invented. rules.suppression_note: Computed by dmi_research.detailed_inflation.resolution: 27 suppressed cells, but at most 9.4% of the rule's possible total is unobserved and the bound is at most 0.0123% of the expenditure basis. This field grades exposure to suppression only. That these UCCs have no established CE-to-CPI scope treatment is a separate defect recorded by review_status OPEN and by the per-member notes; it is not a suppression problem and must not be conflated with one.
rules.go_no_go_note: Milestone 2 Section 20.1 targets zero unresolved expenditure but forbids distorting the methodology to reach it. The residual is 0.1602 percent of the 6836520 million dollar basis. It is recommended for approval as a known limitation under Section 20.1, with 340915 (0.088 percent) as the single item that would most reduce it if BLS confirms a destination.

track_b.rationale: These UCCs have no established Track-A scope treatment, and with the exception of the one transportation member their Track-B relevance cannot be stated without the same missing evidence. Assigning them a Track-B treatment would be a guess dressed as a finding.

reconciliation_all_cu.identity: transformed_reassign + transformed_combine + transformed_replace + out_of_scope + unresolved == exception_total
reconciliation_all_cu.note: This identity is exact on published values. Suppressed cells are never coerced to zero; they are excluded from every total and are accounted for separately by suppression_status.

track_b_treatment_semantics._note: Milestone 2 section 7. Track B is a research comparison only; section 3.3 forbids treating it as authorization to change Baseline or Core. No inflation calculation is performed in this milestone.
track_b_treatment_semantics.NOT_APPLICABLE: The rule covers no owner-occupied shelter expenditure.
track_b_treatment_semantics.RETAIN_CURRENT_PAYMENT: A contemporaneous household outlay on housing, retained under a payments/HCI-style concept even where Track A excludes or replaces it.
track_b_treatment_semantics.EXCLUDE_CAPITAL_ACQUISITION: Capital acquisition that adds to the housing asset. Excluded from a current-payments measure as well as from Track A.
track_b_treatment_semantics.UNRESOLVED: Track-B relevance cannot be established on the available evidence.

suppression_status_semantics._note: Milestone 2 section 16. These values are computed by dmi_research.detailed_inflation.resolution from published BLS parent aggregates and are asserted equal to the values declared here by tests/test_detailed_inflation_milestone_2.py. They are not hand-graded.
suppression_status_semantics._bound_method: BLS publishes the parent aggregate even where it suppresses child cells. Suppressed children therefore cannot jointly exceed max(0, published_parent - sum_of_published_children) + rounding_bound.
suppression_status_semantics.NONE: No member has a suppressed aggregate in any population.
suppression_status_semantics.IMMATERIAL: Suppressed cells exist but are bounded below both thresholds.
suppression_status_semantics.MATERIAL: Suppressed cells breach a threshold. Section 16 then requires an alternative source, aggregation to a stable level, or a block; the choice is recorded in suppression_disposition.
